Draw the substitution and income effects of a price change

Source: R/price-change.R
plot_price_change.Rd

The diagram behind price_change(): the original and final budget lines, the dashed compensated line, the indifference curves through the bundles, the three bundles themselves, and brackets along the axis of the good whose price changed showing how far the substitution and income effects each move the quantity.

Usage

plot_price_change(
  u,
  b,
  new_px = NULL,
  new_py = NULL,
  method = c("hicks", "slutsky"),
  goods = c("Good x", "Good y"),
  title = NULL,
  subtitle = NULL,
  source = NULL,
  xlim = NULL,
  ylim = NULL,
  panel = "blue"
)

Arguments

u

A function of x and y.

b

The original budget().

new_px, new_py

The new price. Supply exactly one.

method

"hicks" or "slutsky".

goods

Axis labels for x and y.

title, subtitle, source

Passed to labs_econ(); sensible defaults are filled in.

xlim, ylim

Panel limits. Default to a little beyond the widest budget line.

panel

Passed to theme_econ().

Value

A ggplot object. Add econ_masthead() last if you want the block.

Examples

u <- cobb_douglas(alpha = 0.4)
b <- budget(income = 120, px = 3, py = 4)
plot_price_change(u, b, new_px = 6)

plot_price_change(u, b, new_px = 6, method = "slutsky")
